intent: Create a distinctive, high-craft landing page for Du Bonheur that turns its real pâtisserie pedigree, sensory product experience, and Berlin identity into a modern digital experience
businessTruths: Du Bonheur is a real French pâtisserie in Berlin Mitte.
The site must represent real products and the real physical business truthfully.
The digital experience should make visiting, understanding the offer, and reaching the shop easy.

productUnderstanding.productDefinition: A real French pâtisserie and café in Berlin whose digital product must help people understand the craft, evaluate the offer, and confidently visit or buy without fabricating the physical business.
productUnderstanding.productStage: real operating business with digital experience redesign
productUnderstanding.problem: The digital experience must communicate exceptional pâtisserie craft and practical visit value without collapsing into generic luxury-bakery conventions.
primaryUsers: people in Berlin deciding whether to visit the pâtisserie
people evaluating products before a visit or purchase
secondaryUsers: existing customers checking location, opening context, or product offer
primaryJobs: understand why the pâtisserie is worth visiting
reach practical visit or shop information quickly
coreWorkflow: inspect real craft and product evidence
productUnderstanding.valueProposition: Make Du Bonheur's real craft and products legible and desirable online while reducing friction between discovery and a real visit or purchase.
differentiators: real French pâtisserie craft interpreted through its Berlin context
truthful sensory/product evidence rather than generic luxury signalling
a digital experience that treats craft process as product value
productMechanics: real product imagery carries documentary truth
editorial sequencing explains craft and product value
missing signature-product evidence triggers capture instead of synthetic documentary generation
productUnderstanding.intelligenceModel: AI may help plan, edit, and generate supporting non-documentary assets, but it may not fabricate real products or business evidence.
productUnderstanding.trustModel: Real products, place, and business claims must be tied to real sources; synthetic supporting imagery must never masquerade as documentary evidence.
productUnderstanding.riskModel: The experience fails if visual ambition weakens appetite, misrepresents products, or hides practical visit information.
productUnderstanding.governanceModel: Truth-sensitive imagery requires source evidence or new capture; creative approval does not override authenticity constraints.
productUnderstanding.desiredPerception: high-craft, sensory, credible, contemporary, warm, and distinctly Berlin-aware rather than stereotypically Parisian
nonNegotiables: do not fabricate documentary product imagery
let craft matter more than generic luxury signalling
constraints: real asset availability may limit final product imagery
commercial priority between shop conversion and in-store visits remains partly unresolved
opportunitiesToBreakConvention: make real pastry construction and texture drive the experience logic
combine French craft with Berlin restraint instead of Paris nostalgia
unknowns: which product photos are licensed and high resolution
whether online shop conversion or in-store visits is the primary commercial goal
assumptions: real product/café evidence can be sourced or captured before final production

evidence.claim: Du Bonheur is a real French pâtisserie in Berlin and must be represented truthfully.
The digital experience should make the craft, offer, and visit action understandable.
Real signature products require real-source treatment; missing documentary assets require capture.
The category is crowded with beige luxury, centered serif, Paris cliché, and generic product-grid treatments.
The desired journey moves from identity/sensory hook through craft and products toward visit or shop action.

antiPrinciples: Do not default to generic beige luxury.
Do not use decorative Paris clichés.
Do not fabricate signature products as documentary imagery.
Do not add motion merely to signal premium quality.

opportunityGaps: make pastry texture and process tactile online
combine French craft with Berlin restraint
use real-product editorial cropping instead of category clichés
unresolvedUnknowns: which existing product photos are licensed/high-resolution
whether online shop conversion or in-store visits are the primary commercial goal
